title: How Japan Pays Gamblers Without Gambling #shorts

lines.text: In Japan, gambling for cash is illegal, and yet people walk out of pachinko halls with cash every single day.
Here's the trick. You win a bucket full of little silver balls.
The hall isn't allowed to give you money, so it swaps your balls for a weird little prize, like a tiny gold bar sealed in plastic.
Then you walk out the door, around the corner, to a tiny window where you can't even see a face.
You slide the prize in, and cash slides back out.
Then a third company buys the prizes from the window and sells them right back to the hall.
A new guy watching says, "Wait. So the prize just goes around in a circle?"
The regular just grins. "It's not gambling. It's shopping."
You see, the law only looks at each step on its own.
A hall gives you a prize. Legal. A little shop buys a prize from you. Also legal.
It's like you hand your friend a sandwich, and he hands you five bucks. Nobody said the word sale.
So a giant industry runs on three buildings standing really close together.
And all three of them pretend they've never met.
